newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt offers 5 airport projects to private sector.
newsitem.headline: Egypt offers 5 airport projects to private sector.

text.p: Egypt's Civil Aviation Authority on Wednesday offered five new airport projects to the private sector under build, operate and transfer agreements.
The airports would be at the oases of Dakhla, Bahariya, Farafra and east Oweinat in the western desert and at the tourist resort of Dahab on the Gulf of Aqaba coast.
The deadline for applications is May 31.
The Civil Aviation Authority has already offered two other airport projects to build, operate and transfer operators -- Marsa Alam on the Red Sea coast and El Alamein on the Mediterranean.
The government is negotiating with the Kuwaiti company Mohamed Abdulmuhsin Kharafi and Sons on the Marsa Alam project, expected to cost about 120 million pounds ($35 million).
In the case of El Alamein, the authority has extended the deadline for bids to January 30.
On January 20, the Egyptian parliament passed legislation making it possible for the private sector to build or operate airports in Egypt under build, operate and transfer schemes.
